subject: Re: Model shortlist & token profile — Westbridge onboarding
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@westbridge.com>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: cto@westbridge.com
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Model shortlist & token profile for onboarding

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. To help our kickoff next week, here's a concise snapshot of our workload and what we need from Redwood to finalize model selection and sizing:

- Use case: Document Q&A + summarization for customer support knowledge base (PDFs, Word, HTML)
- Expected traffic (week 1 ramp): ~8k unique users/day; steady-state target 25k users/day
- Average requests/user: 2.1 requests/session; peak concurrent requests ~350
- Typical prompt length: 600 tokens (extracted context + user question)
- Average expected generated tokens per request: 120 tokens
- Documents: avg 3,200 tokens per doc; expect to index ~45k docs initially

Our questions:
1) Recommended model shortlist for a production rollout that balances latency and cost (we care about 99th pct latency < 750ms for single-turn Q&A)
2) Context window sizing — we need guidance on whether 8k, 16k, or 32k is appropriate given our doc sizes
3) Rough token-volume estimate & cost profile for 1 month at the stated steady state

Attached is a sample token profile export from our analytics (token_profile_spreadsheet.xlsx) and a short security note.

Can we get a recommended shortlist + a simple sizing table before our kickoff on 2027-11-08? Also loop in any ops/infra constraints we should know.

Thanks,

Alyssa Chen
Head of Product
Westbridge Financial
Attachment: token_profile_spreadsheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@westbridge.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & token profile for onboarding

Hi Alyssa — thanks, this is very helpful. Summary answers and a recommended path below; attaching a compact model_profiles_summary.pdf and the sizing worksheet we used.

Quick recommendations (shortlist):
- Redwood-3.8-fast (8k) — baseline: good latency, lower cost; recommend for canary and initial traffic
- Redwood-3.8-long (16k) — primary candidate if you want better long-context extraction without heavy retrieval
- Llama-4o-32k-q8 (quantized) — for archival/long-read jobs where we batch and can accept slightly higher tail latency

Context window guidance:
- Given avg doc = 3,200 tokens and Q&A use case, 16k gives headroom to include multiple doc extracts + prompt. 8k will work if you rely heavily on retrieval and chunking; 32k adds cost but simplifies multi-doc chains.

Token volume estimate (steady-state 25k users/day):
- Requests/day ≈ 25k * 2.1 = 52,500
- Input tokens/day ≈ requests * avg prompt tokens (600) = 31,500,000
- Output tokens/day ≈ requests * 120 = 6,300,000
- Total tokens/day ≈ 37.8M -> ~1.13B tokens/month

Cost profile (high-level):
- Redwood-3.8-fast (8k): best per-token cost; estimated monthly inference cost (including 10% overhead for retries) ~ $X (we'll run exact calc in the sheet)
- Redwood-3.8-long (16k): ~1.35x cost of fast but reduces retrieval ops
- Llama-4o-32k-q8: ~0.9x cost if heavily quantized but higher latency and more engineering ops

Operational suggestions:
- Start canary on Redwood-3.8-fast, run with 10% of traffic, validate latency and hallucination rates for 2 weeks
- If multi-doc answers cause retrieval complexity, upgrade to 16k during rollout
- Use prefix caching on FAQ and high-traffic docs to shave token counts

Next steps:
- I attached the pricing/sizing sheet and model profiles (model_profiles_summary.pdf). Please review and confirm which traffic partition we should canary (10% or 25%).
- Can Marcus (cc) advise on any Dedicated capacity constraints for 11/08 kickoff?

Best,

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachment: model_profiles_summary.pdf (1.2MB)
Attachment: westbridge_sizing_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-11-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Model shortlist & token profile for onboarding

Neha — a couple operational notes to flag before kickoff:

- Latency SLO: For 99th pct <750ms we should limit batch window to 20–30ms and target shards on NVLink-connected instances. Redwood-3.8-fast can hit the SLO at modest scale but monitor token-size variance.
- Autoscaling: recommend a warm pool (reserved capacity) for the canary ramp to avoid cold-start-induced tail latency; we can attach a small Dedicated pool for the first 72 hours of rollout.
- Quantization: Llama-4o-32k-q8 is great for cost, but QA for retrieval-heavy prompts — some semantic drift reported on compressed KV caches. Plan for a comparative quality eval.

I'll prepare a brief ops checklist for the kickoff with exact autoscale thresholds and fallback model routes.

—Vivek
